gap: No result ChatGPT got states that named reviewers who mounted a security camera inside a feeder case found it could not focus on birds a few inches from the lens. Paste's Jim Vorel got clear footage at about 1–2 ft and blurry footage at a few inches, and Digital Camera World's Adam Juniper listed 'Security cameras can't focus closely enough' as a con. It also does not state that TechGearLab measured a Blink Outdoor 4 losing 12% of its battery in 4 days of constant motion, which works out to about a month at a busy feeder instead of the advertised two years.
standout_why: I compared against the cited Wyze pages (Is 24/7 Local Recording going away, Cam v3 continuous recording) and the cited Blink pages (Local Storage with Sync Module, Storage Options). Of these I opened only the Wyze 24/7 page and the Blink Local Storage page; the other two are judged from their titles. All of them cover how to record without a plan, and none has a reviewer's focus or battery result. ChatGPT's own answer only said 'Many security cameras aren't designed for extreme close-ups' and 'test the focus distance', with no named tester and no figure. The uncited PopSci list (2023) is a roundup of dedicated feeders, not a test of Blink or Wyze cameras.
decides: This supports 'yes, but'. You can keep it subscription-free with Wyze microSD or Blink Sync Module 2 USB storage. But a stock security camera a few inches from the perch films blurry birds, so Wyze owners should add Wyze's $9.98 Close-up Lens or mount the camera about 1 ft from where birds land. Blink Outdoor 4 owners should expect battery changes about monthly at an active feeder (TechGearLab's figure), so a solar panel or wired power is the realistic setup. It favours Wyze plus the close-up lens when someone owns both.

findings.product: Ring Stick Up Cam in Wasserstein case
findings.label: Close-range focus, hands-on test
findings.value: Clear HD at about 1–2 ft; blurry video of birds feeding a few inches away; reviewer advises placing the camera about 1 ft from the feeding area
findings.source_title: Paste Magazine – Wasserstein Smart Bird Feeder review (Jim Vorel, 2023-01-30)
findings.note: Paste's Jim Vorel tested only a Ring Stick Up Cam, on a pole about 9 ft up. Blink and Wyze were listed as compatible but not tested. Distances are the reviewer's estimates, not a measured focus chart.

findings.product: Ring Stick Up Cam in Wasserstein case
findings.label: Battery life at a busy feeder
findings.value: about 1 week per charge at more than 100 bird visits per day
findings.source_title: Paste Magazine – Wasserstein Smart Bird Feeder review (Jim Vorel, 2023-01-30)
findings.note: Jim Vorel's estimate from his own feeder traffic; not a timed drain test.

findings.product: Wasserstein Bird Feeder Camera Case (Ring Stick Up tested)
findings.label: Close focus verdict
findings.value: Con: 'Security cameras can't focus closely enough'; birds sat closer than the Ring's nearest focus distance, so even the tray lip was not fully crisp
findings.source_title: Digital Camera World – Wasserstein Bird Feeder Smart Case review (Adam Juniper, 2023-04-04)
findings.note: Adam Juniper tested only a Ring Stick Up. The same review lists the case at 1 kg, with a 2 kg max load and 195 × 180 × 231 mm. Field of view given: Ring 150°, Blink Outdoor 110°.

findings.label: Battery drain under constant motion
findings.value: 12% in 4 days; about a month or a little more on the standard two lithium AA cells (Blink claims two years)
findings.note: TechGearLab ran the camera for 4 days with constant motion, which is close to busy-feeder conditions. 12% in 4 days extrapolates to about 33 days; TechGearLab says 'a little over a month'. Alkaline cells lasted 4 days in their test.

findings.label: Motion detection range test
findings.value: Detected at 2, 5 and 10 ft; failed at 15 and 20 ft
findings.note: TechGearLab's walk test with a person, not birds. Overall score 57, #18 of 20; Video Quality 6.1/10; 1080p; 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi only.

findings.label: Live view latency
findings.value: under 1 second for video; audio about 2 seconds behind
findings.source_title: TechGearLab – Wyze Cam v3 review (Nick Miley, 2023-11-13)
findings.note: Measured by TechGearLab. Overall 80; Recorded Video Quality 7.5; Monitoring 7.8; 130° horizontal FOV; 1080p; microSD slot.
